findings.problem: `review` has no wing selector even though drafts may exist in multiple project, topic, and shared wings. It is unclear which drafts are reviewed and how `keep` selects them; the per-wing journal design does not resolve this.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit `--wing` to `review` and define whether `keep` handles one wing per digest, or specify an all-wings digest and corresponding locking/journal behavior.

findings.problem: Filename collision checks exclude archived notes. A new draft can reuse the filename of an archived draft, and a later `drop` can rename over the existing archive entry, losing the recoverable note.
findings.suggestion: Include the archive namespace in collision checks, or define unique archive filenames and require refusal rather than replacement on collision.

findings.problem: `drop` and `merge` do not define how their draft arguments identify a wing or resolve a title versus filename. Identical names can exist in different wings, so the commands can target the wrong note or cannot be implemented safely; self-merge is also not ruled out.
findings.suggestion: Define an unambiguous target syntax including wing and state, reject paths and reviewed/archive targets where inappropriate, and explicitly refuse merging a draft into itself.

findings.problem: `--new` is said to create a note despite overlap when the title differs, but titles that normalize to the same filename still collide and no alternate filename rule is provided. Thus a valid `--new` request cannot reliably create the requested note.
findings.suggestion: Define a collision-safe suffix or identifier for `--new`, or state that normalized-name collisions remain refusals and adjust the `--new` behavior and acceptance criteria accordingly.

summary: The remaining gaps concern multi-wing review scope, archive data loss on filename reuse, ambiguous mutation targets, and contradictory `--new` filename behavior.
